reader_question: How many people work for newspaper publishers?
grade_line: Documented: Census Bureau counts of employers and their payrolls
title: Newspaper publishers employed 91,350 people in 2023, less than a quarter of the 401,373 they employed in 1998.
reading_guide: The shaded area is the count itself: its height in any year is the number of people on newspaper publishers’ payrolls that March.
measure_line: Paid employees of newspaper publishers, print and online, each March, United States, 1998 to 2023. The count starts in 1998, the first year County Business Patterns sorted businesses by the North American Industry Classification System.
notes: Employment peaked at 413,951 in 2001 and fell in every year after that.

County Business Patterns counts paid employees in the pay period that includes March 12 at businesses classed as newspaper publishers. The count leaves out freelancers, the self-employed and newsrooms in other industries, among them news sites that publish only online, which the Census Bureau classes in another industry.
The industry kept its code, 511110, and its title through the code revisions of 2002, 2007, 2012 and 2017.
alt: Area chart of paid employees at newspaper publishers each March from 1998 to 2023. The count rose to 413,951 in 2001, then fell in every year to 91,350 in 2023, less than a quarter of the 401,373 in 1998.

table.caption: Paid employees of newspaper publishers, each March

chart_notes: The shaded area and the line along its top give the number of paid employees each year. The scale runs from 0 to 500,000.
notes_internal: Maker B, round 1. Data plan row 21, rule 14.35. Domain D01 from the sidecar (News, records and public information); no state named.

Checked by script against census-cbp-newspaper-publishers.csv: 1998 401,373; 2023 91,350; 91,350 / 401,373 = 0.228, less than a quarter; peak 413,951 in 2001; no year from 2002 to 2023 rose over the year before, so 'fell in every year after that' holds.
Grade line opens with H08's grade word, Documented (D3-83 pattern). County Business Patterns comes from the Census Bureau's Business Register, so the line says counts, not a survey.
H09: the measure line gives the window's start with its reason; the sidecar's breaks_in_series now states the 1998 NAICS start from the Bureau's methodology page (R-B1 landed).
The source line is the sidecar's printed_source_line (left out of the spec, D3-102).
Notes 2 and 3 restate the sidecar's qualification in plain words.

Data lead DL-B6 applied: note 2 says online-only news sites sit in another industry (Internet publishing, 519130, under the 2017 code list the 2023 file uses), so the decline is not read as all news jobs. The code's scope rests on NAICS 2017's definitions, not read on census.gov today; request R-B1 asks the research lead to add it to the sidecar.
